recognize_zh: 視野中大多數紅血球呈橢圓形至長桿狀（elliptocytes），部分仍保有中央淡染區，缺乏破碎紅血球、球形紅血球或明顯大小不均，符合遺傳性橢圓形紅血球症（hereditary elliptocytosis）。
features: Majority of RBCs are oval to elongated elliptocytes, some rod/cigar-shaped
Many elliptocytes retain central pallor, indicating normochromic cells
Relatively uniform cell size without marked anisocytosis
No significant schistocytes, spherocytes, target cells or teardrop cells
Scattered platelets; no nucleated RBCs or inclusions seen
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a striking predominance of elliptical and elongated rod-shaped erythrocytes, accounting for the majority of red cells in the field. The elliptocytes are relatively uniform in size and many retain central pallor. Schistocytes, spherocytes, teardrop cells and red cell inclusions are not evident, and platelets appear present. In an asymptomatic young adult, findings are consistent with hereditary elliptocytosis.

ddx.vs: Iron deficiency shows hypochromic microcytic cells with anisocytosis and only occasional pencil cells, not a uniform population of normochromic elliptocytes.
SAO shows stomatocytic macro-ovalocytes with one or two transverse bars or slits, rather than slender elliptocytes with preserved central pallor.
HPP shows marked microspherocytes, fragments and bizarre poikilocytes with very low MCV in addition to elliptocytes.
Acquired conditions show mixed poikilocytes such as dacrocytes, leukoerythroblastosis or dysplastic granulocytes rather than a pure elliptocyte population.
